title: Keemiscomock
summary: Keemiscomock is recorded by William Wallace Tooker as a small brook dividing the shores of Saghtekoos, also known as Apple Tree Neck, in Islip. The same brook was also called Weepoose.
address_label: Sagtikos / Apple Tree Neck, Islip, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate general marker for Saghtekoos / Apple Tree Neck based on Tooker entry 119 and Bayles; exact brook course remains uncertain.
history_content: The history relies on Richard M. Bayles and cautions that no earlier authority had been found, and that Bayles could not recall where he obtained the name. The placename is useful, but it needs careful citation and location review.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted Keemiscomock as a secret enclosed place or a place of refuge. He breaks the name into a word for secret and a second element meaning enclosed place.

Weepoose is kept as a related brook name and may connect with Seapoose, interpreted as little river.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are “mnemonic” devices for Indigenous peoples. As an oral society, the names chosen for geographical sites carry history, traditional environmental/ecological knowledge, navigational information, and teachings - using Indigenous names keeps all of that information alive.”

— Bob Joseph, The Relationship Between Indigenous Peoples and Place Names (2016), Article paragraph 11
land_loss_content: Keemiscomock preserves a small-waterway name in the Sagtikos and Apple Tree Neck landscape while also showing how fragile some references are. Mapping it generally keeps the name visible without pretending the exact brook has been identified.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is an approximate general point for the Sagtikos or Apple Tree Neck landscape in West Islip/Bay Shore, giving broad orientation to the brook landscape rather than a surveyed boundary.
